summary: Asked about greatness, Jesus places a child in the middle and requires disciples to turn and become lowly. He warns against causing ‘little ones’ to stumble, commands radical action against one's own sources of harm, and pictures a shepherd seeking one wandering sheep. Community repair begins with private truth-telling and widens only as necessary. Jesus promises presence among a small gathered body, then answers Peter's limit on forgiveness with an incalculable number and a parable about released debt refused to another.
whyItMatters: This is Matthew's most sustained teaching on life inside the gathered community. Greatness becomes responsibility for the vulnerable; discipline aims to regain a sibling rather than expose an enemy; authority operates under Jesus's presence; and forgiveness received but not extended becomes self-contradictory.

context.author: Anonymous narrator arranging the fourth major discourse
context.audience: A gathered community dealing with status, harm, wandering members, conflict, and forgiveness
context.setting: A house or private teaching setting in Galilee
context.literaryForm: Symbolic action, warnings, lost-sheep image, restoration procedure, promise, and debt parable

outline.heading: A child in the middle and true greatness
A process for regaining a sibling

keyVerses.text: and said, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you turn and become as little children, you will in no way enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
keyVerses.why: The answer to a rank question is conversion toward dependent, unranked lowliness.

keyVerses.text: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
keyVerses.why: The stated goal of confrontation is recovery, beginning with the least exposing step.

keyVerses.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there I am in the middle of them.”
keyVerses.why: Jesus promises presence inside the demanding work of communal discernment, not only in a small worship service.

questions.question: Does ‘become like children’ mean innocent, trusting, or teachable?
questions.answer: Jesus explains his comparison with ‘humble himself’ and places a socially dependent child in the center of an adult rank dispute. Ancient children were loved but lacked adult status and power. The point is not romantic innocence; it is relinquishing claims to greatness and receiving the low-status person in Jesus's name.

questions.question: Who are the ‘little ones’?
questions.answer: The phrase begins with the child and widens to vulnerable or easily disregarded disciples who believe in Jesus. It should not be narrowed to children only or spiritualized so completely that children disappear. Community greatness is measured by whether those with less power are received and protected from harm.

questions.question: What is a ‘stumbling block’?
questions.answer: Skandalon is a trap trigger or obstacle that causes a fall. In Matthew it can name temptation, destructive influence, or conduct that leads another into ruin. The warning is especially severe toward powerful people who endanger little ones, while the eye-and-hand images first direct radical scrutiny toward one's own harmful agency.

questions.question: Why is verse 11 absent or footnoted in many editions?
questions.answer: The sentence ‘the Son of Man came to save that which was lost’ is missing from early major Greek witnesses and likely entered Matthew from Luke 19:10 or a familiar liturgical tradition. The surrounding lost-sheep paragraph still teaches the Father's will that none of the little ones be lost.

questions.question: Is the conflict process a license to confront every issue rigidly?
questions.answer: Its aim is explicit: ‘you have gained your brother.’ It begins privately, adds only one or two witnesses, and involves the assembly after refusal. Power differences, abuse, crimes, and safety can require immediate outside protection rather than private confrontation. A restorative sequence must not become a shield for secrecy or retaliation.

questions.question: What does treating someone ‘as a Gentile and a tax collector’ mean?
questions.answer: It marks that the person no longer participates as a reconciled community member; boundaries are real. Yet Matthew has already shown Jesus calling a tax collector and praising Gentile faith. The phrase cannot mean hatred or permanent dehumanization. Even exclusion remains under a mission of truth and possible restoration.

questions.question: Does ‘two or three gathered’ mean any two people can bind heaven?
questions.answer: The phrase echoes the witnesses just named and sits inside accountable communal discernment. Jesus promises his presence where a small group gathers in his name for this work; it is not a blank check for a private faction. Binding and loosing must align with the Father's will, the search for the lost, and the forgiveness that follows.

questions.question: Is Peter told to forgive seventy-seven times or seventy times seven?
questions.answer: The Greek can be understood either way, and English editions differ. Both numbers answer Peter's proposed seven with a number too large for moral bookkeeping and echo Lamech's escalating vengeance in Genesis 4. Jesus reverses the arithmetic: disciples do not track mercy toward a final permitted refusal.

glossary.def: Children and vulnerable or low-status disciples whom the community is commanded to receive and protect.
The gathered community involved in accountable discernment and restoration.
In this chapter's debt parable, an enormous unit of money, not a personal ability.
